title: DEFINITIONS
previewText:
Airport reference point (or points)

The "airport reference point" (or "points") is a point (or points) within the boundaries of each major airport, as indicated on the flight obstruction area maps for each such major airport. The point or points applicable to each major airport are set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).

Airport referenced imaginary surfaces

blocks.plainText: Airport referenced imaginary surfaces

blocks.html: "Airport referenced imaginary surfaces" include the horizontal surface, the conical surface, the approach surfaces and the transitional surfaces.

blocks.html: Approach surfaces
blocks.plainText: Approach surfaces

blocks.html: The "approach surfaces" are imaginary inclined planes, trapezoidal in shape and located symmetrically with respect to the extended center line of any runway.  Such approach surfaces, extending from both ends of any runway, consist of contiguous inner and outer sections whose dimensions are as follows:
blocks.plainText: The "approach surfaces" are imaginary inclined planes, trapezoidal in shape and located symmetrically with respect to the extended center line of any runway. Such approach surfaces, extending from both ends of any runway, consist of contiguous inner and outer sections whose dimensions are as follows:

blocks.html: (a)        The plane of the inner section:
blocks.plainText: (a) The plane of the inner section:

blocks.html: (1)        begins at a line drawn parallel to, and at the same elevation as, the end of the runway, and at a distance, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline, of 200 feet from the end of the runway;
blocks.plainText: (1) begins at a line drawn parallel to, and at the same elevation as, the end of the runway, and at a distance, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline, of 200 feet from the end of the runway;

blocks.html: (2)        extends for a distance of 10,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;
blocks.plainText: (2) extends for a distance of 10,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;

blocks.html: (3)        has a width of 1,000 feet measured along the line described in paragraph (a)(1) of this Section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway centerline) to a width of 4,000 feet at the outer edge of such inner section, as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this Section; and
blocks.plainText: (3) has a width of 1,000 feet measured along the line described in paragraph (a)(1) of this Section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway centerline) to a width of 4,000 feet at the outer edge of such inner section, as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this Section; and

blocks.html: (4)        rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 50 feet of horizontal distance.
blocks.plainText: (4) rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 50 feet of horizontal distance.

blocks.html: (b)        The plane of the outer section:
blocks.plainText: (b) The plane of the outer section:

blocks.html: (1)        begins at the outer edge of the inner section;
blocks.plainText: (1) begins at the outer edge of the inner section;

blocks.html: (2)        extends for a distance of 15,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;
blocks.plainText: (2) extends for a distance of 15,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;

blocks.html: (3)        has a width of 4,000 feet commencing at the outer edge of the inner section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway center line) to a width of 8,500 feet at the outer edge of such outer section; and
blocks.plainText: (3) has a width of 4,000 feet commencing at the outer edge of the inner section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway center line) to a width of 8,500 feet at the outer edge of such outer section; and

blocks.html: (4)        rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 40 feet of horizontal distance.
blocks.plainText: (4) rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 40 feet of horizontal distance.

blocks.html: Conical surface
blocks.plainText: Conical surface

blocks.html: The "conical surface" is an imaginary inclined surface extending upward and outward from the periphery of the horizontal surface, which:
blocks.plainText: The "conical surface" is an imaginary inclined surface extending upward and outward from the periphery of the horizontal surface, which:

blocks.html: (a)        rises at a slope, measured in an imaginary vertical plane passing through the airport reference point (or points), of one foot for every 20 feet in horizontal distance; and
blocks.plainText: (a) rises at a slope, measured in an imaginary vertical plane passing through the airport reference point (or points), of one foot for every 20 feet in horizontal distance; and

blocks.html: (b)        is measured on a horizontal radius from the airport reference point (or points), and extends for a distance set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).
blocks.plainText: (b) is measured on a horizontal radius from the airport reference point (or points), and extends for a distance set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).

blocks.html: Established airport elevation
blocks.plainText: Established airport elevation

blocks.html: The "established airport elevation" is the elevation above mean sea level of the highest point of the usable airport landing area for any major airport.  The elevation applicable to each major airport is set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).
blocks.plainText: The "established airport elevation" is the elevation above mean sea level of the highest point of the usable airport landing area for any major airport. The elevation applicable to each major airport is set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).

blocks.html: Flight obstruction area
blocks.plainText: Flight obstruction area

blocks.html: The "flight obstruction area" comprises all areas of land or water below the airport referenced imaginary surfaces for each airport.
blocks.plainText: The "flight obstruction area" comprises all areas of land or water below the airport referenced imaginary surfaces for each airport.

blocks.html: Horizontal surface
blocks.plainText: Horizontal surface

blocks.html: The "horizontal surface" is an imaginary horizontal plane, circular or elliptical in shape, which:
blocks.plainText: The "horizontal surface" is an imaginary horizontal plane, circular or elliptical in shape, which:

blocks.html: (a)        is located at a height of 150 feet above the established airport elevation for any major airport; and
blocks.plainText: (a) is located at a height of 150 feet above the established airport elevation for any major airport; and

blocks.html: (b)        is measured on a horizontal radius from the airport reference point (or points), and extends for a distance set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).
blocks.plainText: (b) is measured on a horizontal radius from the airport reference point (or points), and extends for a distance set forth in Section 61-41 (Airport Reference Point, Established Elevation and Specified Radii).

blocks.html: Transitional surfaces
blocks.plainText: Transitional surfaces

blocks.html: The "transitional surfaces" are imaginary inclined planes extending upward and outward from the side edges of all approach surfaces, and from lines parallel to, 500 feet from, and at the same level as the center line of each runway, which:
blocks.plainText: The "transitional surfaces" are imaginary inclined planes extending upward and outward from the side edges of all approach surfaces, and from lines parallel to, 500 feet from, and at the same level as the center line of each runway, which:

blocks.html: (a)        rise at a slope of one foot in height for every seven feet of horizontal distance measured in a vertical plane at right angles to the center line of the runway; and
blocks.plainText: (a) rise at a slope of one foot in height for every seven feet of horizontal distance measured in a vertical plane at right angles to the center line of the runway; and

blocks.html: (b)        extend to the point of intersection with the horizontal surface or the conical surface.
blocks.plainText: (b) extend to the point of intersection with the horizontal surface or the conical surface.

subsections.label: (a)
subsections.plainText: (a) The plane of the inner section:

(1) begins at a line drawn parallel to, and at the same elevation as, the end of the runway, and at a distance, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline, of 200 feet from the end of the runway;
(2) extends for a distance of 10,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;

(3) has a width of 1,000 feet measured along the line described in paragraph (a)(1) of this Section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway centerline) to a width of 4,000 feet at the outer edge of such inner section, as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this Section; and
(4) rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 50 feet of horizontal distance.

subsections.label: (b)
subsections.plainText: (b) The plane of the outer section:
(1) begins at the outer edge of the inner section;
(2) extends for a distance of 15,000 feet, measured horizontally along the extended runway centerline;

(3) has a width of 4,000 feet commencing at the outer edge of the inner section, which increases uniformly (with respect to the extended runway center line) to a width of 8,500 feet at the outer edge of such outer section; and
(4) rises at a slope of one foot in height for every 40 feet of horizontal distance.
